cities.name: Newcastle
cities.tagline: Surf city of ocean baths, working harbour, and Hunter Valley access
cities.general: Newcastle mixes a busy harbour with surf beaches, ocean baths, coastal forts, cafe streets, and quick access to the Hunter Valley wine region.
activities: Swim at the Bogey Hole or Merewether Baths
tips: Weekend trains from Sydney are practical
Book Hunter tastings ahead in peak season

cities.name: Wollongong
cities.tagline: Escarpment-backed beach city south of Sydney
cities.general: Wollongong sits between surf beaches and the Illawarra Escarpment, with coastal cycling, lookouts, hang-gliding sites, rock pools, and easy access to Royal National Park and Kiama.
tips: Sea Cliff Bridge parking is limited
Trains make it easy from Sydney

cities.name: Geelong
cities.tagline: Corio Bay waterfront gateway to the Bellarine and Surf Coast
cities.general: Geelong is a waterfront base for the Bellarine Peninsula, surf towns, wineries, heritage streets, and the start of many Great Ocean Road itineraries.
activities: Continue toward Torquay and the Surf Coast
tips: A car helps connect peninsula stops
Combine with a Great Ocean Road route

cities.name: Byron Bay
cities.tagline: Surf beaches, lighthouse walks, hinterland villages, and whale views
cities.general: Byron Bay is a north coast town known for beaches, surf, the Cape Byron lighthouse walk, whale migration views, food markets, and rainforest hinterland drives.
activities: Surf or swim at patrolled beaches
tips: Parking is tight in peak season

cities.name: Coffs Harbour
cities.tagline: North coast stop for beaches, forests, islands, and marine wildlife
cities.general: Coffs Harbour sits where forested ranges meet beaches and marine parks, with headland walks, island views, family attractions, and access to Dorrigo rainforest.
tips: Dorrigo is cooler and wetter than the coast

cities.name: Albany
cities.tagline: South coast harbour town of granite cliffs, beaches, and Anzac history
cities.general: Albany anchors Western Australia's south coast with King George Sound, granite headlands, white beaches, whale history, and nearby Torndirrup and Porongurup landscapes.
activities: Walk The Gap and Natural Bridge
Drive to Porongurup or Stirling Range
tips: Whale season usually runs through winter and spring
Distances between south coast towns are large

cities.name: Esperance
cities.tagline: Turquoise bays, white beaches, granite islands, and Cape Le Grand access
cities.general: Esperance is a remote south coast base for the Great Ocean Drive, Recherche Archipelago views, Cape Le Grand beaches, and vivid blue water against granite and heath.
tips: Wind and weather can change quickly

cities.name: Ballarat
cities.tagline: Goldfields city of heritage streets, lakes, and Sovereign Hill
cities.general: Ballarat is a Victorian goldfields city with grand architecture, museums, gardens, Lake Wendouree, and living-history experiences at Sovereign Hill.
activities: Visit the Art Gallery of Ballarat
tips: Combine with nearby spa country or Bendigo

cities.name: Bendigo
cities.tagline: Gold rush architecture, galleries, trams, and central Victorian food
cities.general: Bendigo blends gold rush architecture, a strong regional art gallery, heritage trams, gardens, and central Victorian food and wine routes.
activities: Tour the Central Deborah Gold Mine

cities.name: Noosa Heads
cities.tagline: Sunshine Coast beach town beside headland national park
cities.general: Noosa Heads pairs sheltered beaches, surf points, river trips, food streets, and one of Australia's most accessible coastal national park walks.
tips: Parking is limited near the park
Koalas are sometimes visible along the coastal track

parks.name: Royal National Park
parks.tagline: Sydney coastal cliffs, beaches, rainforest pockets, and the Coast Track
parks.summary: Royal National Park protects beaches, sandstone cliffs, rainforest gullies, heathland, and heritage walking routes just south of Sydney.

parks.name: Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park
parks.tagline: Hawkesbury waterways, sandstone lookouts, and Aboriginal rock art
parks.summary: Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park combines drowned river valleys, bushwalks, lookouts, beaches, and important Aboriginal rock engraving sites north of Sydney.

parks.name: Litchfield National Park
parks.tagline: Top End waterfalls, swimming holes, termite mounds, and monsoon forest
parks.summary: Litchfield National Park is a Top End favourite for waterfalls, clear swimming holes, magnetic termite mounds, sandstone plateaus, and dry-season day trips from Darwin.

parks.name: Watarrka National Park
parks.tagline: Kings Canyon sandstone walls, rim walks, and desert oases
parks.summary: Watarrka National Park is centred on Kings Canyon, where red sandstone walls, domes, waterholes, and desert plants make one of the Red Centre's great day walks.

parks.name: Mungo National Park
parks.tagline: Willandra Lakes dunes, deep time, and lunette landscapes
parks.summary: Mungo National Park protects dry lakebeds, sculpted lunettes, Aboriginal cultural history, and World Heritage Willandra Lakes landscapes in far south-west New South Wales.

parks.name: Kalbarri National Park
parks.tagline: Murchison River gorges, wildflowers, and coastal cliffs
parks.summary: Kalbarri National Park spans inland river gorges, natural rock windows, wildflower country, and dramatic Indian Ocean cliffs on Western Australia's Coral Coast.

parks.name: Cape Le Grand National Park
parks.tagline: White beaches, turquoise bays, granite peaks, and kangaroos
parks.summary: Cape Le Grand National Park near Esperance is known for Lucky Bay, granite headlands, Frenchman Peak, heathland, and brilliant south coast water.

parks.name: Stirling Range National Park
parks.tagline: South-west peaks, wildflowers, cloud forests, and Bluff Knoll
parks.summary: Stirling Range National Park protects Western Australia's highest south-west peaks, exceptional wildflower diversity, cloud-prone ridges, and the Bluff Knoll summit walk.

parks.name: Maria Island National Park
parks.tagline: Car-free Tasmanian island of wildlife, fossils, cliffs, and convict history
parks.summary: Maria Island National Park combines wombats, forester kangaroos, fossil cliffs, painted cliffs, beaches, and convict-era Darlington on a car-free island off Tasmania.

parks.name: Booderee National Park
parks.tagline: Jervis Bay beaches, botanic gardens, birdlife, and Aboriginal-managed country
parks.summary: Booderee National Park protects white beaches, coastal heath, marine life, botanic gardens, and Wreck Bay Aboriginal community-managed landscapes on Jervis Bay.

pois.name: Three Sisters
pois.tagline: Blue Mountains sandstone towers above Jamison Valley

pois.name: Wineglass Bay
pois.tagline: Curved white beach below Freycinet granite peaks

pois.name: The Pinnacles Desert
pois.tagline: Limestone spires rising from yellow sand in Nambung country

pois.name: Wave Rock
pois.tagline: Granite cliff shaped like a curling inland wave

pois.name: Cradle Mountain
pois.tagline: Dolerite Tasmanian peak reflected in Dove Lake

pois.name: Katherine Gorge
pois.tagline: Sandstone gorge system on the Katherine River

pois.name: Cape Byron Lighthouse
pois.tagline: Australia's easternmost lighthouse above surf and whale routes

pois.name: Penguin Parade
pois.tagline: Phillip Island little penguins returning at dusk

pois.name: Lucky Bay
pois.tagline: Cape Le Grand beach famous for bright water and kangaroos

pois.name: Dove Lake
pois.tagline: Glacial lake circuit below Cradle Mountain

hikes.name: Bondi to Coogee Walk
hikes.tagline: Sydney clifftop walk linking beaches, baths, and sandstone coves
hikes.summary: The Bondi to Coogee Walk follows Sydney's eastern beaches past cliffs, ocean pools, headlands, and surf clubs.
hikes.start_instructions: Start from Bondi Beach promenade and follow the signed coast path south.

hikes.name: Royal National Park Coast Track
hikes.tagline: Cliff, heath, beach, and lagoon walk between Bundeena and Otford
hikes.summary: The Coast Track crosses Royal National Park's cliffs, beaches, lagoons, waterfalls, and heath between Bundeena and Otford.
hikes.start_instructions: Walk north-to-south from Bundeena ferry wharf or reverse from Otford station.

hikes.name: Grand Canyon Walk
hikes.tagline: Historic loop through rainforest canyon near Blackheath
hikes.summary: The Grand Canyon Walk descends from Blue Mountains lookouts into fern-filled slot canyon, waterfalls, and rainforest before climbing back to Evans Lookout.
tips: Track steps are slippery after rain
Carry a warm layer in the canyon
hikes.start_instructions: Start from Evans Lookout near Blackheath and follow the signed loop.

hikes.name: Cape Byron Walking Track
hikes.tagline: Rainforest, beaches, lighthouse views, and Australia's easternmost point
hikes.summary: The Cape Byron Walking Track loops from Byron Bay through rainforest, beaches, cliffs, the lighthouse, and Australia's easternmost mainland point.
tips: Parking near the lighthouse is limited
hikes.start_instructions: Start near Captain Cook Lookout or Byron Bay beach and follow the signed loop.

hikes.name: Grampians Peaks Trail
hikes.tagline: Gariwerd ridgeline traverse of sandstone peaks and cultural landscapes
hikes.summary: The Grampians Peaks Trail links rugged sandstone ridges, lookouts, waterfalls, camps, and Gariwerd cultural landscapes across western Victoria.
hikes.start_instructions: The full route runs north to south from Mount Zero to Dunkeld.

hikes.name: Wilsons Promontory Southern Circuit
hikes.tagline: Remote beaches, granite peaks, and southern mainland wilderness
hikes.summary: The Wilsons Promontory Southern Circuit links Tidal River, Sealers Cove, Refuge Cove, Waterloo Bay, and remote granite-backed beaches.
tips: Tide and weather affect beach walking
hikes.start_instructions: Start from Tidal River and follow the signed overnight circuit.
